title: Normalized pro-etale scalar-to-tensor and coefficient-pullback identifications
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of commutative rings and let $W$ be a scheme. Use the ordinary unbounded small pro-etale constant-ring module categories and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], in the constant-ring presentation and exact inverse-image convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For finite rings these are the coefficient categories of the cited definition; the same constant-ring constructions below are defined for arbitrary commutative rings. Let $r_W$ be restriction of scalars along $\varphi_W:A_W\to B_W$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Define $C_W=r_W(B_W)$, with its action through $\varphi_W$, and $C_W[0]$ its complex concentrated in degree zero. Write $E_W$ for ordinary sheafified extension of scalars and $M\otimes_{A_W}C_W$ for the sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The pure tensor $b\otimes m$ in $E_WM$ means its image under the actual sheafification unit, not an assertion that every sheaf section is a pure tensor.

Define $e_W:r_WE_W\simeq(-)\otimes_{A_W}C_W$ to be the unique natural isomorphism sending $b\otimes m$ to $m\otimes b$ for every site object and all its sections $b,m$. Apply this isomorphism degreewise and use the degree-zero second-factor total-tensor identification to define the chain isomorphism $e_P:r_WE_WP\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes C_W[0])$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Here $r_W,E_W$ on complexes are termwise.

Let $S_W=(-)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_W}B_W$ be the derived scalar extension with its canonical scalar-derived counit [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Fix a presentation $a_W$ of the ordinary derived tensor with its canonical two-flat-K-flat-representative isomorphism $\rho_{P,H}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $h_W:r_WS_W\simeq(-)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_W}C_W[0]$ by its unique representative normalization: for all flat-term K-flat complexes $P,H$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] [def-pc-kflat-complex] and every quasi-isomorphism $q:H\to C_W[0]$, the composite of $\rho_{P,H}$, $1\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qq$, $h_W^{-1}$, the restriction of the scalar-derived counit on $P$, and the exact restriction localization factor is $Q((1_P\otimes q)\,;\,e_P^{-1})$. The domain of this equality is $Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes H)$ and its codomain is $Q(r_WE_WP)$; the semicolon denotes composition in the displayed order. Thus $h_W$ is selected by the uniquely determining representative property, not by an arbitrary existence of an isomorphism. Here $Q$ is localization from complexes to the ordinary derived category.

For an arbitrary scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, use the canonical constant-ring maps $c_R:f^{-1}R_Y\simeq R_X$ for $R=A,B$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Define $f_A^*C_Y\simeq C_X$ as the inverse of the ordinary restriction/pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] at the $B_Y$-module unit, followed by restriction of the canonical normalized $B$-unit pullback of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. Its normalization sends the inverse-image unit of a section $b$ to $c_B(f^{-1}b)$. Define $L_AQ(C_Y[0])\simeq Q(C_X[0])$ by the exact pullback localization factor, the canonical commutation of termwise pullback with the degree-zero single complex, and $Q$ of this coefficient identification. No boundedness, coefficient flatness, nontriviality or geometric condition on $f$ is imposed.
